context: There are 5 item types, cap = 50, and no limit on the number of copies of a type. Total weight cannot exceed 50. This is a separate capacity-50 example. The single-row update in Figure 14-23 uses capacity 4 and weights 1, 2, and 3. Some item names recur there with different numbers and weights.
description: The table on the left lists item number i, weight wgt[i-1], and value val[i-1], with fruit icons identifying each row. The apple row is light purple and marked “×1.” The banana row is light orange and marked “×2.” Arrows from both lead to the knapsack on the right labeled “Knapsack capacity cap = 50.” The table below combines the input data and counts shown. A 0 means that no arrow selects that item.
The caption states “Maximum value: 290.” Fruit icons show one apple and two bananas using 50 units of capacity.

frames.explanation: From the input, total weight is 10 + 2 × 20 = 50 and total value is 50 + 2 × 120 = 290, matching the caption. If each item were available only once, the optimum on the same input would be a banana and grapes, weighing 20 + 30 = 50 and worth 120 + 150 = 270. This comparison follows from the input and is not drawn. Allowing a second banana raises the maximum to 290.
frames.title: Unbounded knapsack example: each item type can be used repeatedly

summary: Unbounded knapsack permits repeated selections of each type. The figure gives an optimal choice for capacity 50.
